long_biography.plain_text:
León arrived in Miami from Cuba at sixteen, initially taking service and delivery jobs before entering the clinic his father helped establish for Spanish-speaking newcomers. As its first member-services director, he learned managed care from the ground up. Father and son then founded Clínica Asociación Cubana, helped secure Florida’s first HMO license, and built a platform León later bought back after a family sale.

After selling that business in 1994, he founded Leon Medical Centers to serve Medicare patients through integrated outpatient care. The network expanded across Miami-Dade and added hospital coordination and teaching partnerships. In 2022, León launched Leon Health as a Medicare Advantage partner serving the same senior population. He also directed major gifts toward nursing education, geriatric research, cancer care and CasaCuba, joining immigrant health care with the preservation of the community that shaped it.
